title: Rockets beat MI London to reach knockout stage
description: Trent Rockets book their place in the knockout stages of the men's Hundred with a six-wicket victory against MI London at The Oval.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, The Oval

MI London 147-7 (100 balls): S Curran 72 (46); Gregory 2-32

Trent Rockets 148-4 (90 balls): Santner 52* (23); Gleeson 2-27

Trent Rockets won by six wickets

Trent Rockets booked their place in the knockout stages of the men's Hundred with a six-wicket victory against MI London at The Oval.

Rockets' sixth win in seven matches guarantees them a top-three finish as they moved to 24 points at the top - eight more than the trio of Sunrisers Leeds, Welsh Fire and MI London.

Rockets made a shaky start chasing 148 as Finn Allen fell to Tom Curran before Aneurin Donald and Sam Billings also departed, leaving them 46-3 after 30 balls.

Ben Duckett made 27 from 26 balls before he was dismissed by Richard Gleeson halfway through the innings, but Tim David and Mitchell Santner took full advantage of dropped catches - by Sam Curran and Sherfane Rutherford respectively - to steer their side to a sixth consecutive win.

David finished unbeaten on 32, while New Zealand white-ball captain Santner raced to his maiden Hundred half-century from 21 deliveries and struck the winning runs with 10 balls to spare - sealing Rockets' first victory at the Oval in the competition.

Earlier, after being sent out to bat first, MI London made a rapid start, with the in-form Will Jacks, who had three fifties in four matches, looking in ominous touch again - but two brilliant pieces of fielding halted their early momentum.

First, David produced a superb catch running backwards to remove James Vince, before Duckett's pinpoint direct hit while on the floor ran out Nicholas Pooran two balls later to leave the home side reeling at 35-2.

Jacks and captain Sam Curran then undertook a rebuilding job before the opener departed for 39, courtesy of a stunning reflex return catch by leg-spinner Calvin Harrison.

Wickets continued to fall at regular intervals for the hosts, but Sam Curran brought up a 30-ball half-century - finishing with 72 off 46 balls including four fours and five sixes.

He was dismissed on the final ball of the innings as MI London posted 147-7.

It is a crucial Hundred double-header on Sunday as Sunrisers Leeds host Welsh Fire at Headingley, while London Spirit welcome Birmingham Phoenix to Lord's, with the women's games at 11:00 BST and 14:30, and the men's at 14:30 and 18:00 respectively.

The 30-year-old Aussie thought she had a hat-trick when Alice Monaghan was given out lbw, only for the decision to be overturned on review with the ball sliding down leg.

Charley Hull equalled the lowest round in Ladies European Tour history and broke the course record at the Centurion Club to move within one stroke of the lead at the PIF London Championship.

title: Sullivan expected to ignore safety advice and attend West Ham game
description: David Sullivan is expected to attend Saturday's EFL Cup first-round tie against Portsmouth despite being advised to stay away from home matches at the London Stadium.
fullText:
West Ham are expecting David Sullivan to attend Saturday's Carabao Cup first-round tie against Portsmouth despite him being advised to stay away from home matches at London Stadium.

Sullivan, 77, resigned from his position as co-chair of West Ham in June after a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and The Times revealed that seven women have accused Sullivan of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.

He has categorically denied the allegations.

On Monday, a spokesperson for London Stadium told BBC News it had "recommended" to West Ham that Sullivan does not attend matches because of concerns about fan unrest.

London Stadium has asked for advance notice of any planned visits by major shareholder Sullivan - who retains a 38.8% stake in the club - in order to implement additional safety and operational measures.

The match against Portsmouth will be the first the club has played since the allegations against Sullivan were first reported.

The Panorama and Times joint investigation also revealed that Sullivan has been banned from contact with West Ham's women's and youth teams for the past three years because of safeguarding concerns.

London Stadium was unaware of the restrictions until the BBC's report.

Sullivan was banned after a historical allegation about his conduct was raised with the Football Association in 2023. He has previously said the allegation was false.

Sullivan had already been the subject of intense fan abuse for his running of the club, who were relegated to the Championship last season for the first time since 2011.

Although West Ham have stabilised on the pitch, with key figures, including manager Nuno Espirito Santo and skipper Jarrod Bowen committing their future to the club, there remains huge uncertainty off it.

Vanessa Gold, daughter of Sullivan's late business partner and former West Ham co-chair David, backed out of a deal to sell part of her stake in the club to Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky, and instead reached an agreement with Amanda Staveley, the public face of the Saudi Arabia-backed takeover at Newcastle, to sell her entire 25.1% stake.

However, Kretinsky has since sold a small part of his own stake, bringing him under 25%.

That would allow him to buy Gold's shares under West Ham's pre-emption rights rules - which allow existing shareholders first choice to buy shares when they become available.

If he did so he would become West Ham's biggest shareholder, without triggering another clause that would force him to then buy the rest of the club.

It is anticipated Saturday's match against fellow Championship side Portsmouth (15:00 BST) will set an attendance record for an EFL Cup first-round tie, with the Hammers having sold 55,000 season tickets for the new campaign.

title: London submits bid for 2029 World Athletics Championships
description: London submits its final bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships, with the London Stadium, built for the 2012 Olympics, the proposed venue.
fullText:
London has submitted its final bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships.

Athletic Ventures – a body made up of UK Athletics, London Marathon Events, and the Great Run Company – is behind the move to bring the biennial event to the capital and confirmed the final documents have been submitted to World Athletics.

London Stadium, built for the 2012 Olympics and used for the London Diamond League meeting for the past four years, is the proposed host venue.

The host city for the 2029 edition will be confirmed in September.

A feasibility study conducted prior to April 2025, when London's intention to bid was announced, said the competition could bring a £400m benefit to the economy, with the UK government confirming its support for the bid in July 2025.

Championship football team West Ham United, who play their home games at the London Stadium, have also offered their support for the bid.

Hodgkinson & Asher-Smith in GB squad for Europeans

London previously hosted the World Championship in 2017, while Birmingham will host the European Championships this August.

Great Run Company CEO Paul Foster hailed London as "the world's number one sporting city" while UK Athletics CEO Jack Buckner emphasised the importance of the event in the UK's "Olympic legacy".

Buckner said: "Bidding to hold the World Athletics Championships in the London Stadium, the showpiece of London 2012, was always at the centre of the UK's Olympic legacy plans.

"We are very grateful to the government, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport, the Mayor of London, and UK sport for their fantastic support for this bid.

"We're delighted that we have reached agreement with the London Stadium and West Ham United for the use of the London Stadium and our sincere thanks for their commitment in making this happen."

In a statement, West Ham confirmed they are working with London Stadium LLP and Athletics Ventures to support the delivery of the Championships, with a "number of new initiatives that will enhance the stadium and matchday experience for supporters" forming part of the agreement.

The potential impact on their 2029-30 campaign if London's bid is successful is yet to be confirmed.

fullText:
Wayve Uber wins first minicab licence for autonomous cabs from TfL but vehicles will have a safety driver (at first)

The taxi app company Uber and the autonomous technology developer Wayve have been granted the first minicab licences in London allowing them to offer self-driving taxi rides to paying customers – but with a human safety driver in place, for now.

The companies said they would start trips in the UK “later this summer” before the full public launch.

The San Francisco-headquartered Uber and London-based Wayve are racing against the Google-owned Waymo and its Chinese equivalent Baidu’s Apollo Go to launch self-driving taxi services in London. Their progress is being watched closely because the British capital will be one of the first cities in the world to have American and Chinese tech firms operating on the same roads.

Uber and Wayve said more than 100,000 Londoners were on their waiting list for the self-driving taxis.

Transport for London (TfL), the capital’s licensing authority, granted 15 private hire vehicle licences to Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles equipped with Wayve’s artificial intelligence driving software, as well as surround cameras and radar. The companies said TfL had confirmed they reached the required safety standards.

A TfL-licensed private hire driver will sit in the driver’s seat during trips to intervene if necessary, although the software is expected to control the car.

The next step, of operating the taxis without a driver, will require Uber and Wayve to seek approval via a new process, known as an automated passenger services permit, with the government’s Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency.

TfL said it would monitor the use of the vehicles, and was ready to intervene if passenger safety was compromised. A spokesperson said: “Safety is our top priority. Any new vehicle licensed to carry passengers on London’s roads must align with our Vision Zero goal of eliminating all deaths and serious injuries from collisions on London’s streets by 2041.”

Wayve, which was co-founded by the New Zealand-born Alex Kendall, has been testing its tech in London since 2018 with safety drivers. In previous demonstrations to the Guardian the car has navigated most of the obstacles of north London’s busy roads, although the safety driver was forced to intervene at one point.

Sarah Gates, Wayve’s vice-president for global affairs and assurance, said: “This licence is an important step towards giving Londoners the chance to experience autonomous driving technology.

“The responsible deployment of these vehicles will bring us safer, cleaner and quieter streets, and we’re proud to continue working alongside regulators, communities and the public as we take the next steps towards making autonomous rides a reality in the capital.”

The licence approval was not welcomed by minicab drivers, who fear the threat to their livelihood. Matthew Wright, a regional organiser for the GMB union, raised concerns about job losses, increased unemployment and liability for accidents, and said “extreme caution” was warranted from TfL.

“This is a worrying development for our private hire driver members,” he said. “We can’t go charging ahead with new technologies without considering the implications of autonomous vehicles on all parties.”

Driverless taxi services are already operating in several cities around the world, although mainly in the US and China, where most of the software developers are based. However, US companies are essentially blocked from China, and vice versa, meaning they have not had to compete directly.

Uber abandoned its own efforts to develop self-driving technology in 2020, but it is working with several partners around the world who are in turn using different systems. That includes the Chinese company WeRide, which is operating driverless taxis in Abu Dhabi, UAE.

Wayve is also working with the Japanese manufacturer Nissan on integrating its tech in private cars.

The news came as Uber reported better than expected second-quarter gross bookings of $58.02bn (£43bn), but said earnings for the next quarter would fall below Wall Street forecasts.

The company also outlined ‌plans to spend more than $10bn on autonomous vehicles over the coming years, although it did not provide a specific ‌timeline.

title: Brilliant Brook leads Sunrisers to record Hundred score
description: Harry Brook hits a 15-ball fifty and Ryan Rickelton makes 94 not out as Sunrisers Leeds set a new Hundred record, making 241-2 against London Spirit.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Headingley

Sunrisers Leeds 241-2 (100 balls): Rickelton 94* (42), Marsh 76 (37), Brook 55 (18)

London Spirit 204-6 (100 balls): Willey 83* (46); Topley 2-30

Harry Brook shone with a sensational 15-ball fifty as Sunrisers Leeds posted the highest total in Hundred history in their 37-run win against London Spirit.

Having put in to bat at Headingley, opener Ryan Rickelton also struck 94 not out off 42 balls in Sunrisers' astonishing 241-2.

Such was the entertainment provided by Brook and the power shown by Rickelton, Mitchell Marsh's brutal 76 off 37 at the top of the order almost went unnoticed.

On a flat pitch, Marsh and Rickelton added 148 for the first wicket which gave Brook, England's limited-overs captain, the licence to go berserk.

He whacked five sixes and five fours with a combination of power and flair, including a monstrous six over mid-wicket to surpass the previous highest team total of 226.

Brook and Rickelton added 83 off 32 balls for the second wicket as Spirit's bowlers wilted, with the South African stranded short of his century as he was starved of the strike at the close of the innings.

After the carnage inflicted on their bowlers, Spirit made a disastrous start to their reply as Jonny Bairstow fell first ball to Reece Topley, and the rest of the top order also buckled under the pressure as they slipped to 44-4.

But former England all-rounder David Willey performed an admirable rescue act and saved Spirit from humiliation with 83 not out from 46 balls as the visiting side finished on 204-6.

The result takes Sunrisers to fourth in the table and keeps them in play-off contention, but leaves Spirit struggling in seventh.

Sunrisers' 241-2 surpassed Oval Invincibles 226-4 for the highest team total, which they made against Welsh Fire in 2025

Rickelton and Marsh's opening stand of 148 was the highest partnership in The Hundred, beating Jimmy Neesham and Tom Curran's 127 for Invincibles v Manchester Originals in 2023

Brook's fifty was the joint fastest in Hundred history, equalling Adam Rossington's for London Spirit against Northern Superchargers in 2022

Brook's strike rate of 305.55 was the fourth highest for a Hundred innings

Sunrisers hit 21 sixes in their innings (Marsh seven, Rickelton eight, Brook five and Dan Lawrence one). This smashes the previous Hundred record (17)

There were 31 sixes hit overall, the most in a Hundred match – beating the previous best of 29 between Birmingham Phoenix and Trent Rockets earlier this summer

The aggregate total of 445 also beat the record of 418 from that game

For Brook to outshine both Marsh and Rickelton, when the pair were so ruthlessly dominating Spirit's bowlers, indicates just how special his knock was.

Marsh kick-started the innings with his trademark ferocious strength, regularly clubbing the ball down the ground, and by the time he had reached a 24-ball half-century, Rickelton had only faced five deliveries himself.

The Australian fell with only 35 balls left in the innings but there was no respite for Spirit, as Rickelton continued to advance to his fifty off 21 balls before Yorkshire's Brook ignited the lively Headingley crowd.

Spirit's bowlers tried everything, but with no reward. When Jamie Overton perfected his wide yorker, Brook simply reached across and audaciously sliced it over deep third for six.

"That was a masterclass on how to strike the white ball," ex-England captain Michael Vaughan said on BBC Two.

"A few of Harry's shots had a bit of finesse towards the end, but it was just brute power. It's not easy for bowlers, the pitch is very flat, but London Spirit weren't on it.

"He is just brilliant. Sometimes we watch some of his innings in Test cricket and we say, 'Come on, Harry, you're better than that.'

"And we don't really give him the credit for the way that he assesses what the bowler is going to bowl to him, and he's got so many options to every delivery. He is a wonderful player."

title: Sutherland holds nerve as Sunrisers edge past Spirit
description: Sunrisers Leeds beat London Spirit with two balls to spare to keep their slim qualification hopes alive in The Hundred.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Headingley

London Spirit 136-7 (100 balls): Harris 51 (27); Sharma 2-18

Sunrisers Leeds 142-5 (98 balls): Sutherland 37* (21); George 3-25

Sunrisers Leeds won by five wickets

Australia all-rounder Annabel Sutherland led Sunrisers Leeds to a hard-fought win over London Spirit in The Hundred to keep their slim qualification hopes alive.

After a strong start in pursuit of 137, dominated by Phoebe Litchfield's 30 off 17, Sunrisers then lost three wickets for two runs in the space of six balls as Spirit fought back into contention.

But Sutherland added 54 for the fourth wicket with captain Dani Gibson, before a crucial cameo of 13 off five balls from fellow Australian Jess Jonassen got them over the line with two balls to spare.

Sutherland finished unbeaten on 37 from 21 balls which included a stunning pull shot for six to hit the winning runs in style.

Sunrisers' bowlers were also superb in the latter half of Spirit's innings which was fragmented by a rain delay, as Grace Harris' 51 at the top of the order put the home side in danger of conceding an imposing total.

Spirit reached 91-1 off 50 balls before the rain, but proceeded to lose their last six wickets for just 35 runs as Harris and Marie Kelly fell within the first seven balls after the break.

Sutherland chipped in with the big wicket of Marizanne Kapp for 18 while spinners Hannah Baker and Deepti Sharma impressed with two wickets apiece.

The result helps Sunrisers move up to fourth in the table but they are still six points behind Manchester Super Giants in third, while Spirit are on the brink with just one win in five games so far.

title: “London, here I go!” – Vinicius Junior’s agent fuels Arsenal rumours with new social media post
description: Over the last few weeks, there has been increasingly speculation surrounding Vinicius Junior’s future as a Real Madrid player. With less than a year remaining on his contract, talks over a new deal ...
fullText:
Over the last few weeks, there has been increasingly speculation surrounding Vinicius Junior's future as a Real Madrid player. With less than a year remaining on his contract, talks over a new deal are set to resume soon, although there is no guarantee that a positive outcome is reached – and waiting in the wings is Arsenal.

The Premier League champions sense an opportunity to sign Vinicius, whom Real Madrid will look to sell if they cannot agree a new contract with the Brazil international. They are ready to make their move once encouragement has been given by the 26-year-old's camp, with talks having already taken place between the two parties.

And now, more negotiations are seemingly about to take place with a view to an agreement on personal terms being reached. Vinicius is represented by Roc Nation, and as per Diario AS, their president Michael Yormark posted on Instagram over the weekend that he was travelling to London, with the caption "London, here I go. Let's go!"

The emergence of Arsenal's interest has given Vinicius and his representatives leverage ahead of their showdown talks with Real Madrid. An eye-watering offer has already been tabled by last season's beaten Champions League finalists, and the likelihood is that Los Blancos will be asked to match it – or even better it – if they are to secure a renewal agreement in the coming weeks.

However, this tactic does not look like working on Real Madrid. They have already informed Vinicius' camp that the offer on the table is the best one they will get, and if it is not accepted, a sale will be sought this summer. If that happens, Arsenal would be ready to make their move, although they will have to wait until a definitive resolution comes.

title: How Mumbai Indians takeover has affected MI London & Surrey
description: BBC Sport takes a look at what has changed, what has stayed the same and what the future holds for MI London after investment from Indian Premier League side Mumbai Indians.
fullText:
The name has changed, the colours have changed and much of the conversation around the franchise has changed too.

Investment from Indian Premier League (IPL) side Mumbai Indians into Oval Invincibles led to The Hundred's most successful team rebranding itself as MI London and bringing the multi-billionaire Ambani family's cricket empire to The Oval.

Here, BBC Sport takes a look at what has changed, what has stayed the same and what the future holds for the franchise.

Reliance Industries Limited, chaired by Mukesh Ambani, bought a 49% stake in Oval Invincibles in a deal worth about £60m in January 2025, among the first sale of teams in The Hundred.

However, Surrey chief executive Steve Elworthy said their relationship with India's wealthiest family began long before the bidding process got under way.

"They've been huge supporters of The Hundred for a number of years," the former South Africa cricketer told BBC Sport. "They used to take our boardroom box every August to watch The Hundred when we were still Invincibles."

Early conversations convinced Elworthy and his team they had found the right partner in the Ambanis.

"The first meeting we had, we spent about 45 minutes talking about just cricket," Elworthy said.

At about £120m, MI London are the most valuable of the franchises after their London neighbours - the Lord's-based London Spirit, who were valued at about £300m.

What has changed in The Hundred for 2026?

The Hundred 2026 - schedule and how to follow

For the investors, the attraction must have been obvious.

The Oval is one of the world's most recognisable sporting venues, Invincibles had won five titles across men's and women's competitions and Surrey regularly attracts some of the highest attendances in the county game.

"We do cricket well," Elworthy said. "We've got an incredibly strong membership, incredible attendances across formats and we are based in London. It's a really attractive proposition."

As part of the deal, Invincibles were rebranded MI London, bringing the franchise in line with the rest of the MI stable that includes MI Cape Town, MI Emirates and MI New York.

But Surrey, who remain the major shareholder, were determined not to lose their identity.

Elworthy added: "The beauty of this partnership is that the agreement was signed in late 2025 and we are halfway through our first season together, but we haven't even had to look at the contract once.

"We're only looking to make this a success together."

Not much - at least for the players, according to England all-rounder Will Jacks.

"It felt like a very smooth transition for me, having a foot in both camps," Jacks said, when asked about the team's changed identity.

The 27-year-old came through the ranks at Surrey, was part of Invincibles since its inception and also plays for MI in the IPL.

"The kit's changed obviously and it incorporates the blue and gold of MI but the training kit still has the Invincibles colours, so it is kind of a mix of the two," Jacks said.

"So I think they've done a good job of moulding the two together. But for us players and the coaching staff, everything feels very similar."

Tom Moody, who guided Invincibles to a hat-trick of men's titles as head coach, has been replaced by Kieron Pollard, who previously played in the IPL for MI as well as for their sister teams in Major League Cricket, SA20 and ILT20. Skipper Sam Billings has also left, replaced by Sam Curran.

Mitchell McClenaghan also joined from the MI network as the men's bowling coach but there is still a strong Surrey presence in the coaching staff with Gareth Batty, Jim Troughton and Nic Pothas playing prominent roles.

It's a similar story with the women's side where Lisa Keightley, fresh from coaching MI in the Women's Premier League (WPL), succeeded Jonathan Batty but is joined by Surrey women's head coach Johann Myburgh and Dan Helesfay.

Perhaps the biggest additions from the MI investment have come in the form of commercial expertise and global reach.

"MI have got teams around the world and business around the world, so that's something we've learned from them," Elworthy said.

"The Hundred previously was pretty local. Whereas now, I think we've actually got a global brand here and global partners now. That's a brilliant place to be.

"All other teams MI have around the world, they are the sole owners. But they're a minority shareholder here but we don't behave like that. We behave as a team to do the best for MI London."

Former Australia and England coach Keightley echoed Elworthy's words.

"I know MI have been very mindful that for the first time, they're working with another organisation," Keightley said. "From my experience, both organisations are working really hard to make it successful.

"MI's insight from having so many teams is definitely helpful. I know how passionate the owners are and when they commit to something, they do everything to make sure the team's successful."

For players, it also offers a chance to play for other franchises in the MI network and thereby, grow their game.

"I've been very lucky," Jacks said. "Playing with so many great players and icons of Indian cricket at MI has opened me up to a lot of new things and skills. That experience, you can't buy that."

Keightley added: "If you're a MI London player, there's definitely an opportunity to be involved in WPL. Because you build the relationship, you know what a player can do and they know the environment that they're going into."

Their supporters might still be adjusting to the new name and colours but Surrey and MI are already planning for the future.

One important part of their plans will be turning MI London into a brand that exists year-round rather than for just a few weeks each summer.

"You don't want a competition that everybody only thinks about while it's happening," Elworthy said. "It's our job to make sure there's a cycle all the way through the year."

They also plan to take greater responsibility for areas currently managed by the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB).

Having completed the takeover only months before the start of the season, they have relied on ECB to deliver operational aspects, including ticketing.

But Elworthy said the club are currently considering which services they want to take in-house from 2027.

He said: "We want to control and run all the facets of the team - the delivery of the game, the global expansion and building the brand itself."

On the field though, the ambition remains unchanged. After five titles in as many years, MI London's focus is on producing more silverware-winning teams.

That may happen very soon if their men's team can maintain the form which has seen them reach second in the table after five matches.

title: OpenUK Wants Britain to Stop Giving Away Open Source Creations
description: They point to MCP, built by two engineers in London, that ended up under US-based governance.
fullText:
OpenUK recently published its AI Openness report, and buried inside the 40-page document is a big ask from the UK government. Build Britain its own foundation that holds code, governance, and standards the way the Linux Foundation (LF) does in the US.

If you are hearing that name for the first time, OpenUK is a UK-based (obviously) non-profit that advocates for open technology and is led by Amanda Brock. They first put out this call in a report titled "Making the UK the Home of Open Source," which was submitted to UKRI earlier this year.

The AI Openness report restates the case with added urgency this time.

Characterizing the proposed British flavor of LF as a National Foundation, the body, once formed, would hold repositories, standards, and datasets built with UK public money rather than watch that work migrate to servers and governance boards based elsewhere.

It would also handle training, community engagement, and event organizing. Those are areas that would otherwise need separate infrastructure, like an open source program office (OSPO) and a sovereign fund.

OpenUK frames this as a funding and governance gap more than a technology one.

They note that the UK ranks as Europe's top country in open source software and AI openness, yet it has no equivalent to the Linux Foundation, Germany's Sovereign Tech Agency, or China's Open Atom Foundation to show for it.

The non-profit didn't have to look far to prove its point, as MCP is the group's strongest example.

The Model Context Protocol, now the standard behind how AI models connect to outside tools and data, was created by two engineers in London. Anthropic backed the protocol and eventually donated it to LF's Agentic AI Foundation, alongside Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md specification.

In conversation with OpenUK, David Soria Parra, one of MCP's co-creators, said that they gave MCP away because they needed the standard to stay vendor neutral, free of trademark and licensing risk.

If the UK had an established foundation, then they wouldn't have lost MCP to the US. 🙃

The European Commission has already shown off an initiative to break free from US tech dominance by moving towards an open European digital ecosystem. It would cover fields like cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, open hardware, internet technologies, and industrial applications like automotive and manufacturing.

Germany is closer to what OpenUK wants for the UK. Its Sovereign Tech Fund has turned into a government agency, and the report calls that "the right direction."

China has already proven the model works. Open source became a national pillar under its 14th Five-Year Plan, supported by a dedicated foundation called the Open Atom Foundation.

DeepSeek’s R1 showed how that focus pays off, leveraging open-weights and knowledge distillation to deliver frontier-level AI at a fraction of the cost.

OpenUK looks to garner interest from various public sector organizations across the UK while also aiming to collaborate with global experts, delivering the best proposal for their country as a result.
